newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones rises to post biggest weekly gain ever.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones rises to post biggest weekly gain ever.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average closed strong Friday as the blue-chip market racked up its biggest weekly gain ever on upbeat corporate earnings.

The Dow Jones industrial average ended 44.95 points higher at 6,703.55 -- up more than 311.86 points from last Friday's close as the blue-chip market clawed back from a four-week sell-off of 700 points.
The weekly gain was the biggest ever for the 30-stock Dow, beating the 206-point surge in the week of Aug. 2 last year.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,499 to 924 on active volume of 468 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The Nasdaq Composite index also finished higher, gaining 5.50 points to 1,222.57, following strong gains in Microsoft Corp. one day after the it posted much stronger-than-expected fiscal third quarter earnings.
Even as the Dow continued to undo the damage from its month-long slide, analysts were reluctant to predict clear sailing for the market.

"We saw some good bargain-hunting this week, but overall the market was quite mixed," said Eugene Peroni, chief technical analyst with Janney, Montgomery Scott. "I would view this week as an impressive reaction to an oversold market."

Analysts said the relatively strong showings by sectors typically viewed as defensive investments, such as oil and consumer products companies, was evidence of a market still tentative after its recent declines.
The Dow's top gaining stocks were Philip Morris Cos. which gained 2-5/8 to 44-1/4 and Exxon Corp., up 2 to 53-1/2.

"The rally has been fairly narrow, which disturbs us a bit," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker. "This market has to rotate and the cyclicals are going to have to emerge as leadership for this market to get its next leg up."
The narrowness of the rally was most evident among Nasdaq stocks, which managed only modest gains despite Microsoft's stellar 9-1/2 point rally to 107-5/8.

"Point for point, the statistics may show this was one of the best weeks for some of the averages," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "But this wasn't a case where a rising tide lifted all the ships."
Indeed, beyond Microsoft, the performance by even top technology names was unimpressive, with Intel Corp. off 7/8 to 137-1/8 and Cisco Systems Inc. down 1-1/8 to 48-3/8.
The flow of major earnings releases slowed to a trickle on Friday, but even so, investors had plenty to keep them occupied.
Hershey Foods Corp. jumped 1-1/2 to 52-7/8 after the company's first quarter earnings matched Wall Street estimates.

Silicon Graphics Inc. skidded 4-1/8 to 12-7/8. Several investment firms downgraded the shares after the graphics systems company Thursday reported fiscal third quarter earnings sharply below analysts' forecasts.
Russell Corp. tumbled 8-1/2 to 27-1/4 after the leisure and athletic apparel maker company reported lower-than-expected first quarter earnings.
The 30-year Treasury bond rose 5/32, or $1.56 per $1,000 face value, lowering its yield to 7.05 percent from Thursday's close of 7.07 percent. The price and yield move in opposite directions.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 4.57 points to 766.34. The American Stock Exchange index edged up 0.49 to 556.01.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 1.99 to 402.64. The average share was up 20 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,269.466 up 35.905 or 0.50 percent.
